# gitmoap_group_provider_policy (Resource)

Decides which tiers of provider the pipelines in this group and beneath it may run: verified providers, community providers (`disabled`, `verified_only` or `any`), and the organization's own private providers. Platform providers are always accepted. The policy can also require that a newer version's changelog be acknowledged before a provider is upgraded to it. The body replaces the group's policy whole: a field you leave out is inherited from the groups above, unless `override_parent` stops the inheritance here. Answers with the policy now in effect. Owners of the group.

The token needs `provider_policy:manage` and `provider_policy:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_group_by_path" "acme" {
  full_path = "acme"
}

# Which marketplace providers the organization's pipelines may run.
resource "gitmoap_group_provider_policy" "acme" {
  group_id              = data.gitmoap_group_by_path.acme.group_id
  accept_verified       = true
  accept_community      = "verified_only"
  require_changelog_ack = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_id` (String) Group id

### Optional

- `accept_community` (String) Whether an organization's pipelines may run Community-tier providers. `disabled` (the default)
refuses them; `any` admits any Community provider in the catalog; `verified_only` admits only
those whose publisher namespace is verified.
- `accept_own_private` (Boolean)
- `accept_verified` (Boolean)
- `override_parent` (Boolean)
- `require_changelog_ack` (Boolean) When set, moving to a newer provider version requires acknowledging its changelog first. Off
by default.

### Read-Only

- `accepted_tiers` (List of String) The provider tiers this policy accepts in some form. `platform` is always included.
- `inherited` (Boolean)
- `scope_id` (String) The id of the group or repository asked about.
- `source_scope_id` (String) The id of the group or repository whose policy supplied these values — possibly a group
above the one asked about. Absent when no policy is set anywhere and the defaults apply.
- `updated_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--updated_by))

<a id="nestedatt--updated_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `updated_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by its group_id.
terraform import gitmoap_group_provider_policy.example "<group_id>"
```
